summary.ko: 열다·열리다 / 뜨다·펴다 / 개업하다·시작하다 / 열린 / 개방된 / 솔직한
summary.native: to make or become not closed; to start business or an event; not closed; available to all; honest

etymology.ko: 고대 영어 형용사 open에서 왔다. '닫혀 있지 않은, 들어 올려진'이라는 뜻이었고, 게르만 조어 *upana-('위로 올려 둔')로 거슬러 올라가며 up과 관계가 있다. 독일어 offen, 네덜란드어 open과 같은 식구다. 동사는 고대 영어 openian으로, 형용사에서 나왔다. '(가게가) 영업 중인'이라는 뜻은 19세기 초부터 기록된다.
etymology.native: From Old English open, 'not closed, raised up', from Proto-Germanic *upana-, 'put or set up', which is related to up. German offen and Dutch open are close relatives. The verb, Old English openian, was formed from the adjective. The sense of a shop being 'open for business' is recorded from the early 1800s.

grammar.ko: 동사는 타동사와 자동사로 모두 쓴다: I opened the door.(내가 문을 열었다) / The door opened.(문이 열렸다)
grammar.native: The verb is both transitive and intransitive: I opened the door. The door opened.

grammar.ko: 상태는 형용사 open, 동작은 동사 opened로 나타낸다: The shop is open.(영업 중이다) / The shop opened at nine.(9시에 문을 열었다)
grammar.native: Use the adjective open for a state and the verb opened for an action: The shop is open. The shop opened at nine.

grammar.ko: 형용사는 leave, keep과 함께 '목적어 + open' 꼴로 자주 쓴다: leave the door open, keep your eyes open.
grammar.native: The adjective often follows an object after leave or keep: leave the door open, keep your eyes open.

grammar.ko: 형용사 뒤 전치사: open to + 명사(~에게 열려 있다, ~을 받아들이다), open about + 명사(~에 대해 솔직하다).
grammar.native: Prepositions after the adjective: open to (available to, or willing to accept) and open about (honest about).

grammar.ko: 명사형 opening(개업, 개막, 빈자리)과 부사 openly(드러내 놓고)도 자주 쓴다.
grammar.native: Common related forms are the noun opening (a start, a first day, or a job vacancy) and the adverb openly.

meaning.native: to move a door, window, lid, etc. so that it is no longer closed; to become not closed

usage.ko: 닫힌 것을 여는 가장 기본 뜻이다. 사람이 여는 것과 문이 열리는 것에 모두 쓴다. 편지·소포, 컴퓨터 파일·첨부 파일에도 쓴다.
usage.native: The basic sense, used both for a person opening something and for a thing opening. It is also used for letters, packages, and computer files.

examples.text: Could you open the window? It's hot in here.
examples.ko: 창문 좀 열어 줄래요? 여기 덥네요.

examples.text: The door opened, and a young woman came in.
He opened the box and found a watch inside.
examples.ko: 그가 상자를 열어 보니 안에 시계가 들어 있었다.

examples.text: Don't open attachments from people you don't know.
examples.ko: 모르는 사람이 보낸 첨부 파일은 열지 마세요.

meaning.native: to move your eyes or mouth so that they are not closed; to spread out a book, umbrella, etc.

usage.ko: 한국어로는 '눈을 뜨다', '입을 벌리다', '책을 펴다', '우산을 펴다'처럼 동사가 달라지지만 영어로는 모두 open을 쓴다.
usage.native: Used for eyes, mouth, hands, books, and umbrellas. Korean uses several different verbs here, but English uses open for all of them.

examples.text: Open your mouth and say "ah."
When I opened my eyes, it was already noon.
Please open your books to page 25.
It started to rain, so I opened my umbrella.

meaning.ko: (가게·은행 등이 그날) 문을 열다, 영업을 시작하다
meaning.native: (of a shop, bank, museum, etc.) to start business for the day

usage.ko: 가게·은행·박물관이 매일 영업을 시작하는 것을 말한다. 영업 시간을 말할 때 open at + 시각, open on + 요일 꼴로 자주 쓴다.
usage.native: Used for the daily start of business. To give opening times, it often comes with at + a time or on + a day.

examples.text: The bank opens at nine and closes at four.
What time does the museum open on Sundays?
examples.ko: 박물관은 일요일에 몇 시에 문을 열어요?

examples.text: The cafe downstairs opens early for office workers.
examples.ko: 아래층 카페는 직장인들을 위해 일찍 문을 연다.

meaning.native: to start a new business, office, or bank account; (of a new building, road, etc.) to be ready for use for the first time

usage.ko: 사람이 새 가게·지점·계좌를 여는 것(타동사)과, 새 건물·도로·노선이 처음 문을 여는 것(자동사)에 쓴다. 한국어의 개업·개설·개통·개관에 해당한다.
usage.native: Used when people start a new shop, branch, or account, and when a new building, road, or train line is used for the first time.

examples.text: I'd like to open a bank account, please.
The company opened a new office in Busan last year.
examples.ko: 그 회사는 작년에 부산에 새 사무소를 열었다.

examples.text: The new subway line will open in March.

meaning.native: to start a meeting, event, or talk; (of an event or film) to start for the first time

usage.ko: 회의·발표를 어떤 말로 시작하거나, 축제·전시·영화가 처음 시작할 때 쓴다. 무엇으로 시작하는지는 open with + 명사로 말한다.
usage.native: Used when someone begins a meeting or speech, or when a festival, show, or film begins. What comes first is added with open with.

examples.text: The CEO opened the meeting with a short speech.
The film festival opens this Friday.
The movie opens in theaters next week.
examples.ko: 그 영화는 다음 주에 극장에서 개봉한다.

meaning.native: not closed, so that things can go in or out or be seen

usage.ko: 문·창·상자·눈·입이 열려 있는 상태를 말한다. leave, keep과 함께 '열어 두다, 뜨고 있다'로 자주 쓴다. 활짝 열린 것은 wide open이다.
usage.native: Describes a door, window, box, eyes, or mouth that is not closed. It is common after leave and keep. Fully open is wide open.

examples.text: The window is open, so the room is cold.
Please leave the door open when you go out.
I could hardly keep my eyes open during the meeting.
examples.ko: 회의 중에 눈을 뜨고 있기가 힘들었다.

meaning.ko: 영업 중인; 누구나 이용·참가할 수 있는; (자리가) 비어 있는
meaning.native: ready for customers; available for everyone to use, join, or apply for

usage.ko: 가게가 영업 중이거나, 시설·행사·일자리가 누구에게나 열려 있을 때 쓴다. 누구에게 열려 있는지는 open to + 사람으로 밝힌다.
usage.native: Used when a shop is doing business, or when a place, event, or job is available. Who can use it is added with open to.

examples.text: Is the pharmacy still open?
The convenience store is open 24 hours.
The library is open to everyone, not just students.
examples.ko: 그 도서관은 학생뿐 아니라 누구나 이용할 수 있다.

examples.text: The job is still open, so you can apply.
examples.ko: 그 자리는 아직 비어 있으니 지원해도 된다.

meaning.native: honest and not hiding your thoughts or feelings; willing to listen to new ideas

usage.ko: 생각·감정을 숨기지 않는 사람이나, 새 의견을 기꺼이 듣는 태도에 쓴다. be open about(~에 대해 솔직하다), be open to(~을 받아들이다)로 쓴다.
usage.native: Used for people who do not hide their thoughts, or who are happy to hear new ideas. It often comes as be open about or be open to.

examples.text: She is very open about her health problems.
examples.ko: 그녀는 자기 건강 문제를 숨기지 않고 이야기한다.

examples.text: Our manager is always open to new ideas.
examples.ko: 우리 팀장님은 늘 새로운 의견을 잘 받아들인다.

examples.text: I want us to have an open and honest talk.

cautions.ko: 상태를 말할 때 opened를 쓰지 않는다. '가게 문 열었어요?'는 Is the shop open?이다. Is the shop opened?는 틀린 말이다.
cautions.native: Use open, not opened, for a state: Is the shop open? (not Is the shop opened?). Opened is for the action: It opened at nine.

cautions.ko: 회의·파티를 '열다'는 open이 아니다. hold a meeting(회의를 열다), have a party / throw a party(파티를 열다)라고 한다. open a meeting은 모인 자리에서 회의를 시작한다는 뜻이다.
cautions.native: To organize a meeting or party, say hold a meeting or have or throw a party, not open a party. Open a meeting means to start one that people have come to.

cautions.ko: '그랜드 오픈', '오픈카'는 콩글리시다. 영어로는 grand opening, convertible이라고 한다. 동사로 The cafe opened last week.(지난주에 개업했다)라고 하는 것은 괜찮다.
cautions.native: For a big first day, say grand opening, not grand open. A car with a roof that folds down is a convertible. The verb is fine: The cafe opened last week.

note.ko: 누구나 참여할 수 있다, 또는 새 생각을 받아들일 뜻이 있다는 말이다.
note.native: Means that anyone may take part, or that a person is willing to consider new ideas.

patterns.example: The talk is open to the public and free of charge.
patterns.example_ko: 그 강연은 누구나 들을 수 있고 무료다.

note.ko: 숨기지 않고 솔직하게 말한다는 뜻이다. 사람이 주어로 온다.
note.native: Means to speak honestly about something without hiding it. A person is the subject.

patterns.example: He was open about the mistakes he had made.
patterns.example_ko: 그는 자기가 저지른 잘못을 숨기지 않았다.

note.ko: 가게가 몇 시에 문을 여는지 말하는 틀이다. 지금 열려 있다는 상태는 be open으로 말한다.
note.native: Says what time a shop starts business. To describe the state right now, use be open.

patterns.example: The bakery opens at seven on weekdays.

note.ko: 계좌나 계정을 새로 만든다는 뜻이다. 반대로 없애는 것은 close an account다.
note.native: Means to start a new bank or online account. Ending one is to close an account.

patterns.example: I opened an account at the bank near the campus.

difference.ko: unlock은 잠긴 것을 푸는 것이고, open은 문을 열어젖히는 것이다. 문은 먼저 unlock하고 그다음 open한다.
difference.native: Unlock means undoing a lock, while open means moving the door itself. You unlock a door first and then open it.

confusables.example: I unlocked the door but did not open it.

difference.ko: start는 일이나 사업을 시작한다는 넓은 말이다. 가게가 새로 영업을 시작한다는 뜻으로는 open이 더 또렷하다.
difference.native: Start is the broad word for beginning a task or a business, while open is clearer for a shop that begins trading.

confusables.example: They started the business in 2019 and opened the shop last year.

difference.ko: 기계나 전등을 켜는 것은 turn on이다. open은 뚜껑이나 문처럼 실제로 열리는 것에 쓴다.
difference.native: Machines and lamps are turned on, while open is for things that really swing or lift open.

confusables.example: Turn on the laptop and open the file.
